title: SLO-driven predictive load shedding with regional ripple priorities
creator: Priya Nair
description: Design and implement a predictive, SLO-driven load-shedding layer that complements existing admission control and circuit breakers. The goal is to keep p50/p95 latency and error-rate SLOs stable under transient and sustained overload by proactively shedding low-value requests and enabling graceful degradation modes. The system will be region-aware: when a region shows sustained pressure, low-priority traffic is shed locally and preferentially redirected to healthy regions when latency and data residency policies allow. We will use short-horizon forecasting (exponential smoothing) on queue lengths and request mix to trigger shedding earlier than reactive breakers, and maintain strict invariants so high-priority traffic is never dropped unless catastrophic.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive shedding mechanism limits p95 tail latency growth to <20% from baseline during synthetic overload tests
Dashboards show per-priority accepted vs shed counts, regional ripple decisions, and circuit-breaker state
Feature is behind a runtime feature flag and can be disabled in <60s
Automated e2e canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) with rollback on SLO regressions
Unit tests for token bucket logic, forecast module, and region decisioning; integration tests for inter-region fallbacks
implementation_notes: Introduce per-priority short-term token ring: each priority has a reservoir of tokens replenished based on forecasted capacity and SLO targets
Forecasting: use lightweight exponentially-weighted moving average (EWMA) on queue length, request size, and priority mix over 30s/60s windows
Decision path: forecast->admission score->if below threshold either (a) short-circuit with 429 + degrade header or (b) attempt regional reroute if policy allows
Integrate with existing runtime admission controller (ENG-4821) and circuit-breaker states (open/half-open) to avoid conflicting actions
Graceful degradation modes: truncate max tokens, compress structured responses, disable auxiliary tool calls, or substitute cached/stub responses depending on route labels
Config: per-customer and per-route priority mappings, adjustable SLO targets, and percent-of-capacity reserved for high-priority classes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal integration tests and simulation harness (local) - branch feature flag off
Phase 1: Canary in us-west-2 at 5-10% traffic using synthetic overload scenarios - monitor SLOs for 12h
Phase 2: Gradual ramp across additional regions with policy checks for data residency - increase to 30% over 48h if stable
Phase 3: Enable full production traffic for supported routes and provide console controls for manual toggles and per-customer exemptions
Rollback: flip feature flag off, flush token ring state, and trigger circuit-breaker-safe recovery (metrics-based)
observability: Metrics: per-priority accepted, shed, rerouted counts; queue length p50/p95; forecast score; circuit-breaker open-rate
Alerts: p95 latency > configured SLO by 2x for 5m OR shed-rate > 10% for 3m triggers automated rollback window
Dashboards: regional heatmap of shed activity, top routes by shed-volume, customer-level impact summary
Logs: structured shed events include reason, forecast snapshot, tokens remaining, and request fingerprint for debugging
risks: False positives from forecasting could shed valuable traffic — mitigate with conservative thresholds and a warming period
State synchronization lag across regions could lead to inconsistent decisions; design for eventual consistency and prefer local safety-first actions
Increased operational complexity and cognitive load for on-call teams — provide clear runbook and automated diagnostics
Non-deterministic interactions between token rings and circuit breakers could cause oscillation — add hysteresis and cooldown timers
